name: Prototype Exemplars
description: A working collection of visitor surfaces, collaboration instruments, enterprise reference packs, and schema-bearing prototypes for hybrid human-AI teams.

scope: Human collaborators retain purpose, interpretation, publication, and consequential adoption authority.
Repository source retains the accepted structure and version history.

entryPoints.name: Repository orientation
entryPoints.useWhen: The collection map and principal working surfaces are needed.

entryPoints.name: Repository collaboration ground
entryPoints.useWhen: A human or AI collaborator is preparing to assess, plan, write, or change repository material.

entryPoints.name: Context Canvas
entryPoints.useWhen: The work concerns a public-facing page, design input, embedded instrument, or route family.

entryPoints.name: Schema discovery
entryPoints.useWhen: A versioned contract, semantic context, example, source authority, or retrieval route is needed.

entryPoints.name: Planning
entryPoints.useWhen: Prospective options, sequencing, or purposefully deferred terrain enters scope.

entryPoints.name: Threadkeeping
entryPoints.useWhen: A collaboration cycle needs settled rationale, a re-entry position, or decision-changing field observations.

families.name: Prototype Exemplars repository collection
families.description: The repository orientation contract rather than a union of every contained schema.

scope: Repository entry points, schema-family authority, publication routes, and observed uses.

usage.use: Orient a cold collaborator across the repository's schema families and divided authority.
usage.evidenceBoundary: One repository-truthful example exercises the v1 collection contract.
usage.revisitCondition: A new owning family or retrieval state changes repository orientation.

families.name: Context Canvas artifact
families.description: Collection, visitor-surface, prototype-surface, and reference-artifact contracts for the Canvas as visitor surface and design input.

scope: Experience intent, standing, authority, representations, relations, fidelity contracts, and recovery routes.

families.name: Supportive Change Writing collection manifest
families.description: Writing-artifact and documentation contracts incubated through lived repository use until Kindlight Systems establishes the receiving authority.

scope: Writing-artifact meaning and package-local schema interpretation.

usage.use: Validate the existing collection navigation contract without changing package authority.
usage.evidenceBoundary: One real manifest demonstrates current vocabulary and structural compatibility; the use does not normalize the source schema.
usage.revisitCondition: The family moves to Kindlight Systems, gains a canonical identifier, or changes its collection contract.

revisitConditions: A Kindlight Systems schema authority exists.
Observed terminology or extension pressure changes the receiving contract.

families.name: LIMS/ELN Site Reading machine node
families.description: A cross-owner machine-node contract exercised by the integrated functional nucleus while five standalone repositories retain durable source and release authority.

scope: Site Reading machine-node meaning, package-local schema interpretation, and cross-repository instance binding.

families.sourceBand: integrated snapshot with standalone source authorities

relations.note: The downstream program instance binds to the governance schema through the native validator mapping.

usage.use: Exercise a real schema across package and repository roles with its relative dependency closure intact.
usage.evidenceBoundary: One downstream instance demonstrates the cross-owner contract; standalone repositories retain source and release authority.
usage.revisitCondition: The source schema version, common dependency, or public LIMS/ELN publication route changes.

revisitConditions: A Kindlight Systems schema authority exists.
The Site Reading source schema or its dependency closure changes.
The constellation reconciles the five standalone repository authorities.
